summary: The substantive contract attacks are clean: v2 preserves independent per-surface versioning, forbids provider-frame translation, keeps evidence/custody/replay and non-TypeScript roles out of the preview, does not self-admit doctor or SARIF rows, leaves numeric windows reserved, treats schemas.v6 only as an unaccepted candidate, and makes no lock producible before DR-111 closes with evaluable windows and a later DR-103 successor consumes them. Acceptance is withheld because the claimed exhaustive v1-to-v2 change account omits two substantive changed paths. Under the dispatch rule, one SHOULD-FIX requires REJECT.

shouldFix.title: The claimed exhaustive v1-to-v2 change roster omits two substantive changed paths
shouldFix.detail: basedOn.method says v2 contains targeted honesty repairs only at lockJoin, the schemas citation, and reviewGuidance. honestyRepairsFromV1[0] further identifies the removed exact-pin claim's sites as the recordedInputs schemas role sentence and lockJoin. A full recursive comparison also finds substantive edits at /authorityClaim and /purpose: authorityClaim adds the no-lock-by-this-artifact / later-DR-103-successor rule, while purpose adds the universal no-lock-until-evaluable-windows statement and the ID-DEP-4 closure/compatibility clause. Those additions agree with the intended repair and introduce no unsafe lock path, so this is not a blocker; but they are outside the roster asserted to be complete and are exactly the dispatch's silent-path attack.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Amend basedOn.method and honestyRepairsFromV1 to name /authorityClaim and /purpose explicitly and describe their no-lock additions, or revert those two changes. Keep ordinary succession metadata (artifact/version/basedOn/honestyRepairsFromV1) clearly classified as metadata so the next reviewer can reproduce a closed path roster.
